sections.title: The Struggle with Sin
observations: In this section, Paul describes the internal conflict that believers experience between their desire to follow God's law and the reality of sin that dwells within them. He uses the metaphor of marriage to illustrate the believer's relationship to the law, emphasizing that just as a woman is bound to her husband as long as he lives, believers are bound to the law until they die to it through Christ.

Paul's struggle is relatable; he expresses frustration over doing what he hates and not doing what he desires. This highlights the ongoing battle against sin that every Christian faces, illustrating the tension between the new nature and the old sinful nature.

sections.title: The Law and Sin
observations: Paul explains that the law is not sinful; rather, it reveals sin. The law serves to make us aware of our sinful nature. He uses the example of coveting to show how the law can provoke sinful desires, leading to death.

This section emphasizes the purpose of the law: to expose sin and lead us to recognize our need for salvation through Christ. It also underscores the idea that the law, while good, cannot save us; it can only condemn us.

sections.title: The Conflict of Two Natures
observations: Here, Paul elaborates on the duality of the believer's experience. He acknowledges that while he delights in God's law, he also finds another law at work in his members, waging war against the law of his mind.

This conflict illustrates the reality of the Christian life: the presence of sin does not negate the desire to live righteously. Paul’s candid admission of his struggle serves to encourage believers that they are not alone in their battles against sin.

importantVerses.commentary: For we know that the law is spiritual, but I am of the flesh, sold under sin.
Wretched man that I am! Who will deliver me from this body of death?
